name: Chart Spec Builder
blurb: axes, series and scales chosen into a chart configuration
intro: Describe your fields (type, range, number of categories) and the question; it picks the chart, the x/y/colour encodings and the scales (time, band, linear from zero or fitted, log) by Cleveland & McGill's encoding ranking and Few's chart-per-question guidance, explains each decision, and writes the Vega-Lite, Chart.js and ECharts configuration.

inputs.label: Fields
inputs.help: Min/max: numbers, or dates for temporal fields. Distinct values: how many categories.

examples.title: Daily revenue per region over a year

usage: Give fields as rows of {name, type: quantitative|temporal|nominal|ordinal, min, max, distinct}, the goal (auto, trend, compare, ranking, distribution, relationship, part, composition), the row count, an aggregate (sum, mean, median, max, min, none), the library (vegalite, chartjs, echarts), a title and an optional data URL. Returns the chart type, x/y/colour encodings with scale choices, a table of decisions with reasons, warnings (too many colours, log bars, dual axes), and the configuration for all three libraries; result.spec holds the structured choice.
sources: Cleveland, W. S. & McGill, R. (1984), Graphical Perception, JASA 79(387) - ranking of visual encodings
Few, S., Show Me the Numbers, 2nd ed. (2012), chapters on choosing a graph and scales
Histogram bins: Sturges (1926) and the Rice rule
